newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/July index vols down, others up.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/July index vols down, others up.

text.p: Volatilities in July U.S. stock index options were mostly lower Wednesday as the options moved closer to expiration, traders said.
"Volatilities are coming off in July as expected," said one S&P 500 futures-options trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange. "They've firmed up in September a bit."
July S&P 500 futures-options and S&P 100 index .OEX options expire Friday and July S&P 500 .SPX options expire Thursday.
The trader added that some put premiums expanded briefly when the market sold off after rallying solidly off the open.
By about 1130 CDT/1630 GMT, the Dow industrial average .DJI was up 44 points at about 8,020, just off a new session high. The bellwether average hit a session low at 7,953.
Among broader indexes, the S&P 500 .SPX was up 8.31 at 934.07 and September S&P 500 futures gained 8.45 to 940.20.

"This market is all driven by computer technology stocks," one index options trader said, noting that chip maker Intel Corp reported strong earnings late Tuesday and software giant Microsoft Corp was expected to post solid quarterly earnings when it reports Thursday.
The trader added that he expected the rally to continue through Thursday but run into a roadblock Friday as July expirations expire.
He said some institutions, in an effort to bolster their performance, were selling July calls and buying futures.
"As soon as the expiration they'll trigger the sells," he said. "So I think there's going to be another rally tomorrow and then a selloff Friday."
Overall, traders said activity was on the light side, with most of the July activity from investors wrapping up positions ahead of the expiration.
"There's probably a little more position-flattening than trying to get some cheap options" for a quick profit on a sharp market move between now and expiration, the futures-options trader said.
At the Chicago Board Options Exchange, major index options trading was led by the SPX July 925 call, which traded more than 9,300 contracts. The July 935 call traded 6,685.
In the OEX, where a heavy 6,457 July options were exercised Tuesday, turnover was led by the July 910 call, which traded nearly 7,900 contracts.
